concepts.title: Meaning of Accounting: Identification, Measurement, Recording and Communication
concepts.definition: Accounting is the systematic process of identifying economic events, measuring them in money terms, recording them in books and communicating the results to the users who need the information for decisions.
concepts.key_idea: Accounting turns scattered business events into usable financial information through four linked steps: identification, measurement, recording and communication.

concepts.title: Users of Accounting Information
concepts.definition: Interested users of accounting information fall into two groups: internal users such as owners and management who run the business, and external users such as investors, banks, creditors, government and tax authorities who judge it.
concepts.key_idea: Each user reads the same statements with a different question in mind, so accounting information must be relevant, reliable and comparable.

solution_steps.explain: Separate internal users who manage the firm from external users outside it.
Link each user to the decision they take, such as lending, investing or taxing.
Confirm the information is relevant, reliable, comparable and understandable.

concepts.title: Objectives of Accounting: Records, Profit and Financial Position
concepts.definition: The objectives of accounting are to maintain records of business transactions, calculate profit or loss for a period, depict the financial position on a date, and provide accounting information to its users.
concepts.key_idea: Records feed the income computation, which together with assets and liabilities paints the financial position of the entity.

concepts.title: Basic Terms: Assets, Liabilities, Capital, Debtors and Creditors
concepts.definition: Assets are economic resources owned by the entity, liabilities are its payable obligations, capital is the amount invested by the owner, debtors owe money to the firm, and creditors are persons to whom the firm owes money.
concepts.key_idea: The claims on assets come from the owner as capital and from outsiders as liabilities, so assets always equal capital plus liabilities.

concepts.title: Profit and the Change in Closing Capital
concepts.definition: Profit is the excess of revenues over expenses for a period, and it adds to the owner's capital while drawings reduce it, so the closing capital reflects profit earned less amounts withdrawn.
concepts.key_idea: Closing capital equals opening capital plus profit minus drawings, tying the income computation to the financial position.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A business has total assets of {assets} rupees and total liabilities of {liabilities} rupees. Calculate the capital of the owner.

solution_template.explain: Deduct the total liabilities from total assets to get the owner's capital

worked_examples.question_pattern: The assets of a firm amount to {assets} rupees and its liabilities stand at {liabilities} rupees. Find the amount of capital.

solution_template.explain: Deduct the total liabilities from total assets to get the owner's capital

worked_examples.question_pattern: During the year a firm earned revenues of {revenue} rupees and incurred expenses of {expenses} rupees. Calculate its profit.

solution_template.explain: Subtract total expenses from total revenues to get the profit

worked_examples.question_pattern: A trader starts with an opening capital of {opening_capital} rupees, earns a profit of {profit} rupees and withdraws {drawings} rupees for personal use. Calculate the closing capital.

solution_template.action: adjust capital for profit and drawings
solution_template.explain: Add profit to opening capital and deduct drawings to arrive at closing capital
